problems.title: Minimum velocity of a projectile (15 points).
problems.statement: You may ignore the rotation of the Earth. Also assume the earth surface is spherical.

figures.caption: Reference Chart
figures.alt: A globe with dashed equator and central vertical axis; a blue dot on the equator at the right limb, a red arrow labelled V launched from it, and a blue elliptical trajectory arcing over the globe towards the top (north pole).

parts.statement: What is the minimum speed with which a projectile must be launched from the Earth's surface at the equator such that the projectile reaches the north pole?
Find the eccentricity of the trajectory described by the projectile

solution.statement:
### 11.1

[figure: p11-sol-fig1]

[1 point]

$$EM=-\frac{GMm}{R}+\frac12mv^2$$

[1 point]

At points A and B, the $v$ is the same; so, if $v$ is minimum, EM is minimum:

We know that the mechanical energy for an elliptical orbit is given by:

$$EM=-\frac{GMm}{2a}$$

[1 point]

where 2a is the length of the major axis.

Since EM must be minimal, then 2a must be minimal [1 point]

[figure: p11-sol-fig2]

[1 point]

**O:** Center of the Earth and one of the focus of the ellipse.

**F:** the other focus of the ellipse

$$OB+BF=2a$$

[1 point]

$OB+BF=2a$, must be minimal.

F takes an arbitrary position, so to minimize, BF must be perpendicular to OF:

[figure: p11-sol-fig3]

[2 points]

[1 point]

$$OB+BF=R+\frac R{\sqrt2}$$

[1 point]

$$2a=R+\frac R{\sqrt2}$$

This is the minimum value it can take

Correspondingly, the expression for the minimum velocity is

$$v=\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{(1+\sqrt2)R}}$$

[1 point]

Using the M and R values for the Earth, the minimum velocity is

$$v=7195\ \frac{m}{s}$$

[1 point]

### 11.2

Furthermore, $OF=2e\cdot a$, where $e$ is the eccentricity

$$\frac R{\sqrt2}=2e\frac R2\left(1+\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)$$

[2 points]

$$e=\frac1{1+\sqrt2}=0.414$$

[1 point]
